name: Gulf / US–Iran war
value: Iran says 4 tankers hit in Hormuz 11–12 Nov
summary: Iran says 4 tankers were hit by blasts in Hormuz 11–12 Nov; UKMTO reports a ship struck off the UAE; US blockade holds
state: Iran's Revolutionary Guards and army said four tankers were disabled by explosions or mines in the Strait of Hormuz on 11–12 Nov after entering restricted areas; Reuters could not verify the claims (Reuters via GV Wire). UKMTO reported a vessel hit by an unidentified projectile about 14 nautical miles north-west of Ras Al-Khaimah on 11 Nov, causing an engine-room fire. On 10 Nov ADNOC said one of its vessels was damaged in an attack in UAE waters, as the US naval blockade of Iranian ports continued (Arab News). Attacks on Gulf shipping set the Alert.
for_you: UK travellers and seafarers should check FCDO travel advice for Iran and the Gulf states and UKMTO notices. Fuel and freight costs are exposed to disruption in the strait.
rubric_hit: Attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure or shipping (Alert): tankers hit 10–12 Nov, ADNOC vessel damaged; Hormuz traffic restricted

why: Direct hostilities between Iran and the US or Israel threaten Gulf energy infrastructure, the Strait of Hormuz and the wider region.
drivers: Strikes and retaliation, attacks on shipping and Gulf states, mediation and ceasefire talks, US force posture.

rubric.alert: Active strikes between states, attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure or shipping, or the Strait of Hormuz substantially closed.
rubric.watch: A ceasefire or stalemate with sporadic strikes, or credible threats of renewed strikes.
rubric.normal: No direct state-on-state hostilities; diplomacy active.
